config.theme: School PTA budget meeting for next year
config.author: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Code session)

cast.theme: School PTA budget meeting for next year

personas.name: Rebecca
personas.hidden_agenda: Wants the playground painted before her youngest moves on

personas.name: Gloria
personas.goals: Supplies and field trips for the kids
personas.hidden_agenda: Her class missed the zoo trip last year

personas.name: Samir
personas.hidden_agenda: Remembers the pledges, not what was collected

agenda.title: Next steps
agenda.goal: Get the draft ready for the vote

beats.summary: This year's numbers; Samir's walkathon memory is generous
Grants, buses, the playground and the yearbook; Rebecca's teacher count goes unchecked

turns.speaker: Rebecca
turns.text: Hi, everyone. Thanks for staying after pickup. Hiro, could you start us off?

turns.speaker: Hiro
turns.text: Sure. Income was nineteen thousand three hundred, and expenses were eighteen thousand and fifty.

turns.speaker: Rebecca
turns.text: So we ended up a little ahead.

turns.speaker: Hiro
turns.text: A little. The reserve is forty-eight hundred now.

turns.speaker: Gloria
turns.text: That's more than I expected, honestly.

turns.speaker: Samir
turns.text: The walkathon did most of it. I think it brought in about twelve thousand.

turns.speaker: Hiro
turns.text: The pledges were about twelve. What we actually collected was eighty-nine hundred.

turns.speaker: Samir
turns.text: Oh, right. Some families never paid their pledges. That happens every year.

turns.speaker: Gloria
turns.text: Still, eighty-nine hundred from kids walking in circles. That's amazing.

turns.speaker: Rebecca
turns.text: It really is. The kids love it, too.

turns.speaker: Samir
turns.text: My son asked if he could do it twice this year.

turns.speaker: Hiro
turns.text: The other fundraisers were small. The book fair and the spring concert bake sale.

turns.speaker: Rebecca
turns.text: Anything that lost money?

turns.speaker: Hiro
turns.text: The movie night broke even. Nothing lost money.

turns.speaker: Rebecca
turns.text: Fundraisers for next year. I'd keep the walkathon, obviously.

turns.speaker: Samir
turns.text: Could we send pledge reminders this time? It might close the gap between pledged and collected.

turns.speaker: Hiro
turns.text: Yes, please. The online form can send a reminder after a week.

turns.speaker: Samir
turns.text: I'll set up the reminders on the form before the walkathon.

turns.speaker: Gloria
turns.text: The bake sale is a lot of work for what it makes. The teachers end up baking half of it.

turns.speaker: Rebecca
turns.text: Should we drop it?

turns.speaker: Gloria
turns.text: Maybe just make it smaller. Cookies only.

turns.speaker: Hiro
turns.text: The concert families like it, though. It's part of the evening.

turns.speaker: Rebecca
turns.text: Then the bake sale stays, but it's cookies only and parents bring them.

turns.speaker: Gloria
turns.text: Thank you. The teachers will be grateful.

turns.speaker: Samir
turns.text: The new bakery on Elm makes the best cookies I've ever had, by the way. The ginger ones.

turns.speaker: Hiro
turns.text: Is that the one with the blue door? I've walked past it every day.

turns.speaker: Gloria
turns.text: Go in. Trust me. The lemon bars too.

turns.speaker: Rebecca
turns.text: Okay, I'm hungry now. Spending. Classroom grants are a hundred and twenty-five per teacher, and we have twenty teachers, so that's twenty-five hundred.

turns.speaker: Gloria
turns.text: A hundred and twenty-five doesn't go far, but every bit helps.

turns.speaker: Hiro
turns.text: We could raise it to a hundred and fifty with the surplus.

turns.speaker: Rebecca
turns.text: Let's keep it at a hundred and twenty-five this year, and see how the walkathon does.

turns.speaker: Gloria
turns.text: The buses are the thing I really want. Five hundred and twenty a bus, and we lost the zoo trip last year.

turns.speaker: Hiro
turns.text: How many buses would the zoo need?

turns.speaker: Gloria
turns.text: Three. One per class in the grade.

turns.speaker: Hiro
turns.text: That's fifteen sixty. We can do that.

turns.speaker: Rebecca
turns.text: Then the third-grade zoo trip is funded this year.

turns.speaker: Gloria
turns.text: I'll book the zoo date with the office tomorrow.

turns.speaker: Rebecca
turns.text: And the playground. The paint quote was twenty-two hundred.

turns.speaker: Hiro
turns.text: That's half the reserve.

turns.speaker: Rebecca
turns.text: The lines are so faded the kids can't see the hopscotch.

turns.speaker: Samir
turns.text: Could parents paint it on a Saturday instead? We'd just need the paint.

turns.speaker: Hiro
turns.text: Paint is maybe four hundred. Much cheaper.

turns.speaker: Rebecca
turns.text: A parent paint day. I love that.

turns.speaker: Gloria
turns.text: Somebody would need to check the school allows it. Insurance and so on.

turns.speaker: Rebecca
turns.text: I'll ask the principal this week.

turns.speaker: Hiro
turns.text: Yearbooks are fourteen dollars each, and we have two hundred and ten orders so far.

turns.speaker: Samir
turns.text: Do the yearbooks pay for themselves?

turns.speaker: Hiro
turns.text: They do, with a little left over.

turns.speaker: Rebecca
turns.text: Next steps. The vote is on May twentieth.

turns.speaker: Hiro
turns.text: I'll put the draft budget together and send it to the board a week before.

turns.speaker: Gloria
turns.text: Can the draft go home in backpacks too? Not every family reads email.

turns.speaker: Rebecca
turns.text: Yes. Paper copies in the Friday folders.

turns.speaker: Samir
turns.text: Will there be childcare at the vote meeting? Turnout is always low without it.

turns.speaker: Rebecca
turns.text: Thank you, everyone. That was easy. I wish every meeting was like this.
